Cartes.gouv.fr: France's Sovereign Alternative to Google Maps and Waze Adds Street View

2026-07-07 Xavier Martinage, Capital.fr Cartes.gouv.fr, IGN, Géoportail, Google Maps alternative, Street View, sovereign mapping, France, cadastre, LiDAR HD, isochrones, open data
Read the source article

Quick summary

France's sovereign mapping platform Cartes.gouv.fr, successor to Géoportail, now offers a free Street View alternative alongside 1,100+ cartographic layers, 20cm aerial photography, cadastre data, and centimetric LiDAR HD terrain models — positioning itself as a public-sector competitor to Google Maps and Waze.

Key takeaways

  • Cartes.gouv.fr launched June 25, 2026 as successor to Géoportail (IGN), with 1,100+ cartographic layers
  • Offers a free, open alternative to Google Street View with 110 million photographs already integrated
  • Features 20cm resolution aerial photography, IGN vector plans, cadastre, and INSEE data
  • Includes thematic maps for urbanism, environment, and forests
  • LiDAR HD program provides centimetric terrain modeling for hydrology, archaeology, and natural risk prevention
  • Tools include surface/distance measurement, isochrone calculation, and public contribution features
  • Géoportail becomes obsolete in September 2026, making Cartes.gouv.fr the official successor
